answer: Operator-Linked Resource Ledger. Each new identity must consume a scarce shared resource (compute quota, API calls, storage) drawn from the operator's single ledger, and any flagged clone freezes that entire ledger until review. An attacker cannot scale clones without draining one account, so the per-identity marginal cost equals the full ledger lockout, not a small fee. The freeze persists across a glacier of pending requests. Detection runs on a rolling horizon of behavior similarity. A walnut-sized audit sample confirms each freeze, so evasion requires rebuilding fully distinct operators.
